title: Spike the Gemini Live API for Customer discovery
objective: Learn whether a live voice channel is viable for Customer search before E3 commits to an architecture around it.
acceptance_criteria: the spike answers the question it was scoped to ask, in writing
the throwaway code is thrown away, or an ADR explains why it stays
latency and cost are recorded, because those are what decide it
notes:
FREE TIER CONFIRMED TO CARRY THE LIVE API, from the founder's AI Studio rate-limit page on 2026-08-05. Three models are available with unlimited requests per minute and a real token budget: Gemini 2.5 Flash Native Audio Dialog (1M tokens/min), Gemini 3 Flash Live (65K), Gemini 3.5 Live Translate (20K). Veo 3 and Veo 3 Lite read 0/0 and are NOT available. So this is a working spike rather than a written assessment, and the constraint to design against is tokens per minute, not request count — the opposite of the 15-requests-per-minute limit that shapes every other Gemini call in this repository. FOUNDER AUTHORISED FREE TIER ONLY: stop and report rather than calling any paid tier. Native Audio Dialog has by far the largest budget and is the one to start with. Explicitly throwaway. A spike that quietly becomes production is the failure mode; say so in the report rather than leaving it to be discovered. Phase 2 work — the coordinator should not assign it while Phase 1 tasks are open unless the founder asks.

ASSIGNED 2026-08-06 ON THE FOUNDER'S INSTRUCTION, ahead of its priority. The note above says the coordinator should not assign it while Phase 1 work is open unless the founder asks; he asked. The reason it moved is WP-010: description-finished to first estimate measures 2177 ms median against a 2000 ms budget, 8 of 12 runs over, and 1997 ms of that is the model call itself. Whether a live voice channel is viable is no longer a Phase 2 curiosity — it is the question the budget miss raises. Delegation is unavailable (OpenCode weekly limit, resets in 3 days), so this is written in-session; the spend envelope is untouched.
completion_notes:
Question 1 of three — does the ephemeral-token flow work — is NO as tested, so questions 2 and 3 were not run. That is T084's instruction (stop at the first no) and the right use of a free-tier budget: a dialect comparison against an architecture that cannot ship is a number nobody can act on.

The Live surface itself works: a BidiGenerateContent socket opened on gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-preview-09-2025 and replied. POST /v1alpha/auth_tokens returns 200 and a 76-character token. That token is rejected both as ?access_token= (1008) and as ?key= (1007), and the mint returns an identical stub for four different payloads without validating any of them.

So ADR-0009 Option C is unavailable today and Option A stands — nothing needs building. The ADR stays Proposed rather than Rejected: the spike proves the token could not be used, not that it cannot be, and the surface is in preview.

TWO NEAR-MISSES WORTH MORE THAN THE ANSWER. Both model listings (v1beta and v1alpha, 50 models each) show ZERO models supporting bidiGenerateContent — read alone that says Live is unavailable, and it is wrong. And auth_tokens:create 404s while auth_tokens returns 200: the hinge of the whole ADR was one URL suffix away from a wrong answer in the decisive direction. A 404 or an empty listing is evidence about the question asked, not about the world.

Cost: zero. No session completed, so no audio tokens were consumed. Free tier only throughout. Throwaway code was written outside the repository and is gone.

Also corrected in the ADR: its latency premise (645 ms, so Live is not worth adopting for speed) is now false for the path that matters — WP-010 measured 2177 ms against a 2000 ms budget on production.
